clue.text: Exhibit incorporated in case of first offender?

indicators.note: the letters for incorporated sit in the case formed by the name of the first offender

parts.note: Eve, who ate the forbidden fruit, was the first sinner in Genesis

explanation.surface: A piece of evidence is filed away in the dossier on someone convicted for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit a quality is to show or display it plainly, a verb sense shared exactly.

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are thrown about forcefully into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up, then responds with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet leap in which the dancer crosses and beats the calves together in the air.

clue.text: Bury is home to, say, 80,000, or some such number

indicators.note: houses, so the word for bury contains the abbreviation for say

parts.note: to inter is to bury in a grave
eg, for example, stands for say

explanation.surface: The Lancashire town of Bury has a population of around eighty thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town (a place in north-west England), but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number with no fraction, such as eighty thousand, is the mathematical sense.

indicators.note: around, so the word for talk goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a chat is a casual conversation

explanation.surface: Someone discusses the Welsh language versus English.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'welsh' on a bet is to fail to pay up, so the word here is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Welshing on a debt means swindling the creditor, an act of dishonesty.

parts.note: to dump something is to discard it
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone tips a fish dessert into the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet dumpling boiled or baked is a classic British pudding, and some are sweet desserts.

clue.text: Used dinner hour wrongly, becoming this?

definitions.text: Used dinner hour wrongly, becoming this?

indicators.note: incorrectly, so the letters of the three words are set in a different order

explanation.surface: A worker who skipped lunch breaks to do other things ends up underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: misuse your lunch break and you go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deprived of adequate food is underfed, the result of missing meals.

parts.note: PE is physical education
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
severe means harsh or hard

explanation.surface: An army man on a punishing training session is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun, but 'soldier on' means keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly despite difficulty is the shared idiomatic sense.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a boar is a wild pig
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A favourite creature has perished in the English city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the city in north-east England, but it is a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Positioned within the body of a vessel, as of an engine mounted inside the hull.

definitions.meaning: to crush or beat into powder

explanation.surface: Someone takes payment in sterling for doing their everyday job.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush grain is one sense; dull repetitive labour, the daily slog, is the other.

definitions.meaning: with big cannons in operation, read literally as artillery firing

explanation.surface: A triumphant army is described with its modern weaponry.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriving or doing extremely well is the idiom; read literally, big cannons in action.

clue.text: Having made a profit, for instance, in childhood?

definitions.text: Having made a profit, for instance, in childhood?

parts.words: Having made a profit, for instance, in childhood?
parts.note: the phrase means showing a gain on the books, while the childhood hint plays on young children being urged towards behaving well

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a youngster turned a profit early in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in credit by some amount, or ahead financially, is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word for talk is cut off

parts.note: rabbit, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, is British slang for chatter

explanation.surface: A clergyman is accused of droning on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for chattering at length; dropping its last letter leaves the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish scholar and teacher of the law is the spiritual leader of a congregation.

indicators.note: having withdrawn or gone back, so the whole assembled run of letters is read in reverse
the soldier's letters go inside the word the

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman has joined a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the whole soldier-in-the run backwards, not the soldier alone; the crew is a rowing eight, named for its oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat with eight oarsmen, and the oarsmen themselves, are called by the number.

clue.text: Woman in charge is unarmed surprisingly

indicators.note: signals the letters of the two words come out in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes with surprise that the female boss carries no weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny employed to look after children is a woman in charge of them.

clue.text: Climb hill on skis and get a stitch

definitions.meaning: a skier going uphill splays the tips outward, leaving a zigzag V pattern in the snow
an embroidery stitch worked in a zigzag of crossed slanting lines

explanation.surface: A skier labouring uphill ends up with a pain in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch' looks like the cramp of an exhausted climber, but it is the sewing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses take their name from the fish-skeleton pattern of the V-shaped marks.

clue.text: Some Europeans lose marks when it's assessed

definitions.text: Some Europeans lose marks when it's assessed

parts.words: Some Europeans lose marks when it's assessed
parts.note: reads as Germans losing Deutschmarks, or pupils losing marks, but describes money deducted from earnings by the state

explanation.surface: Germans complain of losing money when a valuation is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on earnings calculated by the authorities takes away part of a person's pay.

definitions.meaning: a hollow or ... in the ground

explanation.surface: A burglar feels gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is slang for one sense, and a hollow in a road or field is the other.

indicators.note: the man's name is placed inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a portal is a doorway or gateway
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A picture shows a man standing in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or picture of someone, as a painted likeness, is the shared sense.

indicators.note: incomplete, so the last letter of the archaic pronoun is dropped

parts.note: thou is the old second-person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A runner-up complains they have still not crossed the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal conjunction means however or nevertheless, like yet at the head of a clause.

clue.text: He's bound to upset girl with boo

indicators.note: overturned, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl is upset after being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is legally bound to perform an obligation to another is the term.

parts.note: hip reads as trendy, but it is the hip of a hip-hip-hooray shout led by a girl at a US sports game

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman from the States is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl leading the crowd's chants and the cry of hip, hip, hooray at American sports games.

definitions.meaning: a mooring post or buoy for ships
the mahi-mahi, a sea fish, also bears the name

explanation.surface: A harbour where boats tie up and anglers cast a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring post in a harbour is one sense; the mahi-mahi fish is the other.

indicators.note: the word for payments wraps around the word for pass over

parts.note: doles are handouts or allowances paid out
to omit is to skip or leave out

explanation.surface: Tolls are charged to cross a pass through the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a mountain pass, but 'pass over' is a verb meaning skip.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of limestone peaks in north-eastern Italy, part of the Alps.

indicators.note: lifted up, which in a down clue reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: poor means of low quality
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A substandard ducal banner is hoisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or wilt, a verb sense matched by sagging.

clue.text: Such coordinates used within the Arctic Circle?

definitions.text: Such coordinates used within the Arctic Circle?

parts.words: Such coordinates used within the Arctic Circle?
parts.note: reads as a geographic grid near the North Pole, but names the mathematical system of radius and angle

explanation.surface: Someone asks which map references are used near the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematical coordinates giving distance from an origin and an angle are named after the pole.

indicators.note: dropped, so the abbreviation is taken out of the word for study

parts.note: to peruse is to read carefully
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student quits, having left college with something inherent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by or in itself, inherently.

indicators.note: wild and unrestrained, so the letters of the word tough run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on a hard task.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for aught means anything at all, as in for all I know.

parts.note: to unearth something is to discover it

indicators.note: with its middle removed, so only the first and last letters of lady stay

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a cold-hearted and absurd woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurdly early, as in rising at an ungodly hour, is the informal sense.

clue.text: Deputy to Sergeant-Major, stifling a fit of laughter

indicators.note: smothering, so the deputy and sergeant-major letters surround the single letter

parts.note: a proxy acts or votes on behalf of someone else
SM is the military abbreviation

explanation.surface: A stand-in for the sergeant-major tries to suppress a bout of giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' that looks like part of 'a fit of laughter' is the letter that 'stifling' smothers; the definition is only the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent outburst or spasm of emotion, often used of uncontrollable laughter.

clue.text: In ship, sailors are the most important part

indicators.note: the sailors are placed inside the word for the ship's backbone

parts.note: the keel is the spine of a ship, here standing for the vessel
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Aboard ship, the crew are what matter most.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or essence of something, like the edible seed inside a nut.
